options.text: The joining of two small nuclei to form a larger one
The splitting of a large, unstable nucleus into two smaller nuclei, releasing energy
The emission of an alpha particle from a nucleus
The absorption of a gamma ray by a nucleus

questions.explanation: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a large, unstable nucleus (such as uranium-235 or plutonium-239) into two smaller daughter nuclei, along with the release of two or three neutrons and a large amount of energy. It is the process used in nuclear power stations and nuclear weapons.

questions.stem: What is the role of the moderator in a nuclear reactor?

options.text: To absorb excess neutrons and control the reaction rate
To slow down fast neutrons so they can cause further fission
To transfer heat from the reactor to the turbines

questions.explanation: The moderator (usually water or graphite) slows down the fast neutrons released during fission. Slow (thermal) neutrons are much more likely to be absorbed by uranium-235 nuclei and cause further fission. Without the moderator, most neutrons would be too fast to sustain the chain reaction.
